rv.q: Go in with the right spirit and you'll have a good time.
Theo Ubique's production is still worth a look if for no other reason than to celebrate the life's work of Anzevino.
Together, they’ve transformed a Broadway flop (which closed after just 33 performances) into a joyful, engaging experience for Chicago audiences.
Theo Ubique continues to produce polished, topnotch musicals, and the theatre seems to continually surpass previous productions with each new show.
Whether you’re an anglophile, a fan of Princess Diana, or just like a good musical, “Diana” will not disappoint.
This is a difficult story to tell onstage, and the ensemble is more than up to the task.
It's not deep, but it's fun for what it is.

Tonight's opening of "Diana the Musical" was a wonderful tribute to the man I have been talking about, as it was Fred's vision along with co-director Brenda Didier, to bring this wonderful biography/musical to a Chicago area theater.
Diana’s energy and conviction are the things that give it life and make it gratifying entertainment.

cn.t: Critics find this intimate Chicago production breathes new life into the Broadway flop, with the smaller setting and strong performances elevating the paint-by-numbers biographical material about Princess Diana.
